fieldValues.title: A dispatched issue's stated baseline can already be stale — check the artifact's own git log before trusting the issue text
fieldValues.summary: A dispatch brief restated a prior report's baseline ("diff against census-2026-08-26.json", "four cells with no check") without re-checking it against current master. Both had already moved: a cycle-two run diffed against 08-26 the evening before the issue was filed, and one of the four unguarded cells picked up a check independently. The unit still executed correctly because Ground-stage discipline caught it before Work: `git log --oneline -- <the artifact's own path>` against origin/master, not the issue body, is what surfaces this — the issue and its dispatch comment are testimony about the artifact, not the artifact.
fieldValues.rationale:
Found working srs#635 (grid census cycle two, dispatched 2026-09-06 16:54): the issue's own text and its 17:18 dispatch comment both stated the 08-26 baseline and the four-cell figure from srs#580, itself carried from PR #582's 2026-09-05 report. PR #582 had already run the next cycle the previous evening, and a portability check landed independently between then and now. Neither change was large or hard to find — one `git log` on the census directory and one read of `scripts/checks.json` — but neither the coordinator's dispatch comment nor the issue body caught it, because both were transcribing #580's checklist rather than checking the artifact.

The alternative considered was treating the issue text as authoritative and doing exactly what it asked (diff against 08-26, report four cells) — cheaper in the moment, but it would have produced a report that silently re-litigated ground already covered by #582 and mis-stated the current enforcement gap by one cell, exactly the kind of drift the census exists to catch elsewhere in the corpus.

What generalizes: for any unit whose issue text restates a factual baseline about a versioned artifact (a census cycle, a check-registry count, a corpus statistic), the Ground stage's `git fetch` + read-the-comments discipline is necessary but not sufficient — the artifact itself (its own commit history, its own current file) is the primary source, and the issue is only ever a claim about it as of when it was written.
